# 人 — person

**Strokes:** 2 · **Key (radical):** 人 (no. 9; as a left-hand component 亻, にんべん) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

人 is a pictograph of a person seen from the side: a body with an arm or leg leaning forward. Compare [大](大.md), a
frontal figure with arms spread. As 亻 on the left it marks people and human activity: 休 ([休](休.md)), 住, 作, 体, 何, 他.

Because 人 and 入 ([入](入.md)) are nearly mirror images, they are a classic confusion. In 人 the long left-falling stroke is written first from the top and
the right-falling stroke starts from its middle; in 入 the short left-falling stroke comes first and the long right-falling stroke starts at the top, to its upper left.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ジン | on | [人口](../words/人口.md) じんこう, 日本人 にほんじん, 外国人 がいこくじん |
| ニン | on | 人間 にんげん, 三人 さんにん, 人気 にんき, 職人 しょくにん |
| ひと | kun | 人 ひと, 女の人 おんなのひと, 人々 ひとびと |
| -り | kun | counting one and two persons: 一人 ひとり, 二人 ふたり (special forms) |

Special reading: [大人](../words/大人.md) おとな (adult).

## Common words

- [人口](../words/人口.md) じんこう — population
- [大人](../words/大人.md) おとな — adult
- 人 ひと — person, people

## Notes

人々 ひとびと (people) repeats the kanji with the repetition mark 々 and voices the second ひと.

# 休 — rest

**Strokes:** 6 · **Key (radical):** 人 (as 亻, no. 9) · **Phonetic:** none (an ideographic compound) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

休 combines 亻 (person, [人](人.md)) and 木 (tree, [木](木.md)): a person resting against a tree. This is the standard explanation
and a good mnemonic, even though some details of its early history are debated.
It means "rest", "take a break" and "be off work".

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| キュウ | on | [休日](../words/休日.md) きゅうじつ, 休憩 きゅうけい, 休暇 きゅうか, 定休日 ていきゅうび |
| やす.む | kun | [休む](../words/休む.md) やすむ, お休み おやすみ, 昼休み ひるやすみ |
| やす.まる | kun | 心が休まる こころがやすまる |
| やす.める | kun | 体を休める からだをやすめる |

## Common words

- [休む](../words/休む.md) やすむ — to rest, to be absent
- [休日](../words/休日.md) きゅうじつ — day off, holiday
- 休憩 きゅうけい — break

## Notes

Compare 体 (body), made of 亻 and 本, and 木 itself ([木](木.md)): both are close in shape but not in meaning.

# 何 — what

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 人 (as 亻, no. 9) · **Phonetic:** 可 (カ) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

何 is a phonetic compound: 亻 ([人](人.md), person) and 可 (カ, "can, possible"). In classical Chinese it was an interrogative "what?", "which?",
and the original sense "carry" (later written 荷) is commonly cited for the character. How the "what" use arose from it is not firmly settled, so treat the history as debated.
In Japanese it is the basic question word "what", used also for "how many" before counters.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| カ | on | 幾何 きか (geometry), rare in everyday words |
| なに | kun | 何 なに, [何か](../words/何か.md) なにか, 何も なにも, 何色 なにいろ, 何人 なにじん (what nationality) |
| なん | kun | [何時](../words/何時.md) なんじ, [何人](../words/何人.md) なんにん, 何分 なんぷん, 何歳 なんさい, 何年 なんねん |

## Common words

- [何時](../words/何時.md) なんじ — what time
- [何人](../words/何人.md) なんにん — how many people
- [何か](../words/何か.md) なにか — something

## Notes

- **なに vs なん:** 何 is read なん before the sounds t, d, n (なんでも, なんだ, なんの) and before most counters (何時, 何人, 何分); otherwise なに (何を, 何が, 何か). This is a tendency with exceptions, so learn common words as units.
- 何人 is なんにん "how many people" but なにじん "what nationality".
- Look-alike: 河 (river) and 荷 (load) share the 可 component; 何 has 亻 on the left, and is not [今](今.md).

# 供 — accompany, offer

**Strokes:** 8 · **Key (radical):** 人 (as 亻, no. 9) · **Phonetic:** 共 (キョウ) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

供 is 亻 (person) plus 共 (together, both hands holding something). 共 gives the sound キョウ, and it also seems to contribute meaning: a person who is with you, or who holds something out together with both hands.
It means "accompany, attendant" (お供) and "offer, supply" (供える, 提供). The sense "child" in 子供 is not the kanji's own meaning: see [子供](../words/子供.md), where 供 is treated as an ateji for the suffix ども.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| キョウ | on | 供給 きょうきゅう (supply), 提供 ていきょう (provide), 供述 きょうじゅつ (statement) |
| ク / クウ / グ | on | 供養 くよう (memorial service), 供物 くもつ (offering), 供御 くご (rare) |
| とも | kun | お供 おとも (attendant, escort), 供をする (accompany) |
| そな.える | kun | 供える そなえる (to offer to a god or the dead), お供え おそなえ |
| -ども | kun | [子供](../words/子供.md) こども, 私ども わたくしども |

## Common words

- [子供](../words/子供.md) こども — child
- 提供 ていきょう — provision, offering
- 供給 きょうきゅう — supply (opposite: 需要 じゅよう)
- お供 おとも — attendant, companion on a trip

## Notes

- **供える vs 備える:** 供える offers something to a deity or the dead; 備える (そなえる) is "prepare, equip": 災害（さいがい）に備える. They are different words with the same sound.
- The very common 子供 uses 供 almost only for its reading こども; the spelling 子ども is also widely used.
- **Look-alikes:** 供 vs 共 (together; same right-hand part, no 亻), and 借 (borrow) or 倍 (double), which also share 亻.

# 入 — enter, put in

**Strokes:** 2 · **Key (radical):** 入 (no. 11) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

入 is often described as a pictograph of something pointed going inward (an entrance or tip), but the origin is debated.
Use it as a mnemonic: two strokes converging, opposite to the outward 出 ([出](出.md)).
It means "enter", "go in" and "put in".

It looks like 人 ([人](人.md)) but the strokes differ: the short left-falling stroke is written first, then the long right-falling stroke from the top (人 is the other way round).

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ニュウ | on | 入学 にゅうがく, 入院 にゅういん, 入力 にゅうりょく, 出入国 しゅつにゅうこく |
| ジュ | on | rare, e.g. 入内 じゅだい |
| い.る | kun | 入る いる (literary or in set phrases): 気に入る きにいる |
| い.れる | kun | 入れる いれる (put in), 入り口 いりぐち |
| はい.る | kun | 入る はいる (enter), 入口 → 入り口 |

## Common words

- [入口](../words/入口.md) いりぐち — entrance
- [出入口](../words/出入口.md) でいりぐち — entrance/exit
- 入る はいる — enter

## Notes

Opposite: [出](出.md). Compare 入る はいる (enter) and 入れる いれる (put in).

# 出 — go out, exit

**Strokes:** 5 · **Key (radical):** 凵 (no. 17, "open box") · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

The common explanation is a foot (止) stepping out of a pit or cave (凵). The modern shape looks like two stacked
山 ([山](山.md)) but is not formed from them. It means "go out", "come out", "put out" and "emerge".

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| シュツ | on | 出発 しゅっぱつ, 出席 しゅっせき, 輸出 ゆしゅつ, 出入国 しゅつにゅうこく |
| スイ | on | rare, e.g. 出納 すいとう |
| で.る | kun | 出る でる (go out), [出口](../words/出口.md) でぐち, 家出 いえで |
| だ.す | kun | 出す だす (put out, send), 取り出す とりだす |
| い.でる | kun | literary, e.g. 出で湯 いでゆ |

## Common words

- [出口](../words/出口.md) でぐち — exit
- [出入口](../words/出入口.md) でいりぐち — entrance/exit
- 出る でる — go out, appear, attend

## Notes

Opposite: [入](入.md). Pairs: 出入り でいり, [出入口](../words/出入口.md), 出入国 しゅつにゅうこく.

# 励 — encourage; be diligent

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 力 (no. 19), at the right · **JLPT:** N1 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

励 covers both encouraging someone and diligently applying oneself. [励む](../words/励む.md) はげむ means "work hard; strive," while [励ます](../words/励ます.md) はげます means "encourage; cheer someone on." [激励](../words/激励.md) げきれい is encouragement that spurs someone on.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Notice a 厂-like cover over [万](万.md)-shaped strokes, beside [力](力.md), "strength." Imagine putting strength into effort or encouragement. This is a visual memory aid, not a historical derivation; the 万-like shape does not contribute "ten thousand" to this meaning.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| レイ | on | [激励](../words/激励.md) げきれい — encouragement; spurring on |
| はげ.む | kun | [励む](../words/励む.md) はげむ — work hard; strive |
| はげ.ます | kun | [励ます](../words/励ます.md) はげます — encourage; cheer someone on |

All three sourced readings are retained in the practice selections. The app groups kun-readings with the same stem before the dot, so はげ.む supplies the はげむ question; はげ.ます remains in the reading table but does not create a separate question. The on-reading question is れい. In 激励, 激 supplies ゲキ and 励 supplies レイ.

励ます is a plain dictionary form, despite ending in ます. Its polite form is 励まします (はげまします). The polite form of the separate verb 励む is 励みます (はげみます).

## Common words

- [激励](../words/激励.md) げきれい — encouragement; spurring on
- [励む](../words/励む.md) はげむ — work hard; strive
- [励ます](../words/励ます.md) はげます — encourage; cheer someone on

## Notes

- [劣](劣.md), "inferior; worse," has 力 below [少](少.md) rather than at the right. Making an effort does not itself mean being inferior.
- [万](万.md), "ten thousand," resembles part of the left side, but lacks the cover and right-hand 力 of 励.
- [厚](厚.md), "thick; cordial," also has a 厂 overhang, but a different interior and no right-hand 力.
- [努](努.md), [勉](勉.md) and [勤](勤.md) share effort or diligence meanings. They are useful comparisons, not clearly wrong alternatives to that side of 励's meaning.
- Distinguish the roles: 勉強に励む (べんきょうにはげむ), "work hard at one's studies," versus 友達を励ます (ともだちをはげます), "encourage a friend." Neither effort nor encouragement guarantees success.

# 勉 — strive, exert effort

**Strokes:** 10 · **Key (radical):** 力 (no. 19) · **JLPT:** N4 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

勉 conveys exertion or diligent effort. Its most useful beginner word is 勉強, "study."

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** spot [力](力.md), "power," at the lower right and imagine putting effort into a difficult task. This is a modern memory aid; it does not identify a historical phonetic component.

## Readings

The table focuses on ベン. The source also records つと.める; it is not needed for the common words below.

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ベン | on | [勉強](../words/勉強.md) べんきょう — study; 勤勉 きんべん — diligent |

## Common words

- [勉強](../words/勉強.md) べんきょう — study; 勉強する — to study
- 勉強会 べんきょうかい — study group or study meeting
- 勤勉 きんべん — diligent; hard-working

## Notes

勉 is normally encountered in compounds, not as an independent everyday word for studying. [学](学.md) also concerns learning, while 勉 highlights effort.

Do not confuse 勉 with [動](動.md), "move": both include 力, but their other parts differ.

# 募 — recruit; solicit

**Strokes:** 12 · **Key (radical):** 力 (no. 19) · **JLPT:** N2 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

募 concerns seeking people, applications, or contributions. 募集 ぼしゅう is recruitment or taking applications, and 募金 ぼきん is fundraising. The native verb 募る つのる also describes a feeling growing stronger.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Picture the 艹-shaped top, 日-shaped center, and spreading lower strokes above 力, as though gathering many people's efforts.

The canonical indexing radical is 力 at the bottom, not the conspicuous 艹-shaped top.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ボ | on | [募集](../words/募集.md) ぼしゅう - recruitment; taking applications |
| つの.る | kun | 募る つのる - grow stronger; solicit contributions or participants |

## Common words

- [募集](../words/募集.md) ぼしゅう - recruitment; taking applications
- 募る つのる - solicit; grow stronger
- 応募 おうぼ - application; entry
- 募金 ぼきん - fundraising

## Notes

- The recruiting side 募集する seeks applicants; the applicant 応募する responds. These compounds share 募 but describe different sides of the process.
- 募る has both intransitive and transitive uses: 不安が募る ふあんがつのる, anxiety grows, versus 参加者を募る さんかしゃをつのる, seek participants. The particle and context distinguish the uses.

# 口 — mouth

**Strokes:** 3 · **Key (radical):** 口 (no. 30) · **JLPT:** N4 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

口 is a pictograph of an open mouth. It extends naturally to openings: an entrance or exit is a "mouth", and the
word for "mouth" counts persons ("mouths to feed" is the usual explanation for the 人口 sense).
As a key it appears in kanji about speaking, eating, and sound: 味, 吸, 叫, 吐, 呼, 咲.

The outer box in 国 and 回 is the enclosure 囗 (くにがまえ), a different key, not a mouth.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| コウ | on | [人口](../words/人口.md) じんこう, 口座 こうざ, 口頭 こうとう |
| ク | on | 口調 くちょう, 異口同音 いくどうおん |
| くち | kun | 口 くち, [出口](../words/出口.md) でぐち, [入口](../words/入口.md) いりぐち, 口癖 くちぐせ |
| -ぐち | kun (voiced) | 非常口 ひじょうぐち, 改札口 かいさつぐち |

## Common words

- [出口](../words/出口.md) でぐち — exit
- [入口](../words/入口.md) いりぐち — entrance
- [出入口](../words/出入口.md) でいりぐち — entrance/exit
- [人口](../words/人口.md) じんこう — population

## Notes

Compare 日 ([日](日.md)), which is also squarish but taller, with a line across the middle.

# 告 — announce; inform

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 口 (no. 30) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

告 is about making something known. It appears in [報告](../words/報告.md) ほうこく, "report," and 広告 こうこく, "advertisement."
The verb 告げる つげる means to tell, inform, or announce; it directs attention to the information being conveyed.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** use the 口 at the bottom as the mouth making an announcement, with the strokes above as a sign attracting attention. This is not historical evidence.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| コク | on | [報告](../words/報告.md) ほうこく — report; 広告 こうこく — advertisement |
| つ.げる | kun | 告げる つげる — tell; announce |

## Common words

- [報告](../words/報告.md) ほうこく — report
- 広告 こうこく — advertisement
- 告げる つげる — tell; inform

## Notes

Compare the upper part with [古](古.md), which has only 十 above 口.
The upper strokes also resemble [牛](牛.md), but the whole 告 has a separate box below.
[報](報.md) is a useful meaning partner in 報告, not an opposite.

# 女 — woman, female

**Strokes:** 3 · **Key (radical):** 女 (no. 38) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

女 is a pictograph of a kneeling figure with crossed hands. As a key it appears in many kanji about women and family: 母, 姉, 妹, 好, 姫, 嫁.
In 好 (like), 女 and 子 (child) are commonly explained as mother and child. Component meanings are a historical layer, not a description of the word today.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ジョ | on | [男女](../words/男女.md) だんじょ, 女性 じょせい, 彼女 かのじょ, 少女 しょうじょ |
| ニョ | on | 老若男女 ろうにゃくなんにょ |
| ニョウ | on | 女房 にょうぼう |
| おんな | kun | 女 おんな, 女の子 おんなのこ, 女の人 おんなのひと |
| め | kun | 女神 めがみ, 女滝 めだき |

## Common words

- [男女](../words/男女.md) だんじょ — men and women
- 女性 じょせい — female (formal/polite)
- 女の子 おんなのこ — girl

## Notes

Opposite: [男](男.md). 女 can read おんな or め; 女の子 is the everyday word for "girl".

# 日 — sun, day

**Strokes:** 4 · **Key (radical):** 日 (no. 72) · **Phonetic:** none (not a phonetic compound) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

日 is a pictograph of the sun. The oldest forms are round, often with a dot or short line inside; brush and carving
styles squared the circle. What the inner mark originally represented is uncertain, so treat any story about it
(a sunspot, a core) as a mnemonic rather than established fact.

The same word covers both "the sun" and "a day" (one sun-cycle), which is why one character serves for both
and for the days of the week and the month (日曜日, 十日). As a component, 日 usually hints at the sun, daylight or time,
as in 明 (日 + 月, bright), 時, 晴, 昨.

It is easy to confuse with 目 (eye, taller with two inner lines), 白 (white, one extra stroke on top) and [月](月.md) (moon, slimmer, with two inner strokes).

- 買う is a regular godan verb: 買います, 買わない (note the わ, not あ), 買って, 買った.

# 励ます (はげます) — encourage; cheer someone on

## Meaning

励ます means encouraging or cheering someone on or up. In the ordinary person-encouragement use, the person takes を.

- 友達を励ましました。 (ともだちをはげましました。) — I encouraged my friend.
- 友人の言葉に励まされました。 (ゆうじんのことばにはげまされました。) — I was encouraged by my friend's words.

The second sentence is passive: 励まされる (はげまされる) means "be encouraged." The speaker receives encouragement rather than encouraging someone else.

## How the kanji combine

[励](../kanji/励.md) writes はげ, with ます in kana. Here ます is part of the dictionary-form spelling, **not a polite ending**. This is one native godan verb ending in す, not a compound of on readings.

Useful forms are 励まします (はげまします), 励まして (はげまして), 励ました (はげました) and 励まさない (はげまさない). Compare the separate verb [励む](励む.md) (はげむ), "work hard," whose polite form is 励みます (はげみます).

## Synonyms and antonyms

[激励](激励.md) (げきれい) is a noun for encouragement; 激励する is a related する verb. [応援](応援.md) (おうえん) includes support and cheering, but can also mean practical backup.

[慰める](慰める.md) (なぐさめる), "comfort; console," emphasizes easing distress. 励ます can urge someone onward. Encouragement and consolation may occur together; this is a difference of emphasis, not mutually exclusive compartments.

## Distinctive meaning

Encouragement does not guarantee success or that the recipient immediately feels better. The verb is not restricted to encouraging other people: one can encourage oneself too. This article focuses on encouragement, not the separate voice-raising sense recorded in dictionaries.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1557350, sense 1; comparisons 1253760, 1179840, 1156890 and 1557390. Usage: [Digital Daijisen, 励ます](https://kotobank.jp/word/励ます-600677).

# 励む (はげむ) — work hard; strive

## Meaning

励む means working hard or applying oneself to an activity. In this useful modern pattern, mark the activity with に: 勉強に励む (べんきょうにはげむ), "work hard at one's studies."

- 毎日、勉強に励んでいます。 (まいにち、べんきょうにはげんでいます。) — I work hard at my studies every day.
- 研究に励みました。 (けんきゅうにはげみました。) — I applied myself to research.

## How the kanji combine

[励](../kanji/励.md) writes はげ, and む is the written ending. This is one native verb, not a compound of separate on-reading words.

It is a godan verb ending in む. Useful forms are 励みます (はげみます), 励んで (はげんで), 励んだ (はげんだ) and 励まない (はげまない).

## Synonyms and antonyms

[努める](努める.md) (つとめる), "strive; make an effort," and [努力](努力.md) (どりょく), "effort," overlap with 励む.

Contrast [励ます](励ます.md) (はげます), "encourage; cheer someone on":

- 自分が勉強に励む。 (じぶんがべんきょうにはげむ。) — I myself work hard at my studies.
- 友達を励ます。 (ともだちをはげます。) — I encourage a friend.

These are different roles: applying oneself to an activity versus encouraging someone.

## Distinctive meaning

励む describes effort, not guaranteed success. The activity + に pattern above is the modern teaching model here; it is not a claim that historical dictionaries contain no other constructions.

Do not mistake 励ます for a polite form of 励む. 励む becomes 励みます; 励ます is a separate verb whose polite form is 励まします (はげまします).

# 募集 (ぼしゅう) - recruitment; taking applications

## Meaning

募集 is recruitment or a call for applicants, participants, or contributions. It is a noun and a transitive する-verb. What is being sought takes を: 参加者を募集する (さんかしゃをぼしゅうする), "seek participants."

- イベントの参加者を募集しています。 (イベントのさんかしゃをぼしゅうしています。) - We are recruiting participants for the event.
- アルバイトの募集に応募しました。 (アルバイトのぼしゅうにおうぼしました。) - I applied for the advertised part-time position.

応募する (おうぼする) is applying or responding to the call. In the second sentence, に marks the recruitment opportunity being answered.

## How the kanji combine

[募](../kanji/募.md) contributes soliciting or seeking people and contributions; [集](../kanji/集.md) contributes gathering. Together the related ideas describe seeking people or resources and bringing them together. The on readings are ボ + シュウ.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[集める](集める.md) (あつめる), "collect; gather together," is broader and can also concern people or money. 募集 highlights seeking applications or contributions, not simply picking up objects.

[招待](招待.md) (しょうたい) is an invitation to someone as a guest. English "invitation" can also describe a call for applications, but the Japanese words are not freely interchangeable. 募集 and 応募 describe the seeking and responding sides, not opposites in value.

## Distinctive meaning

募集 is not limited to hiring employees. It can seek event participants or submissions, and the dictionary also records raising funds or contributions: 寄付を募集する (きふをぼしゅうする), "solicit donations." [集金](集金.md) (しゅうきん) concerns collecting money, often payments due; 募集 foregrounds the call for contributions.

A call for applicants does not itself mean that every applicant has been accepted. In finance, 株式の募集 (かぶしきのぼしゅう) concerns offering shares for subscription; this specialized recognition does not turn every use into employee selection.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1514830, senses 1-3; 応募, entry 1180030.

# 勧める (すすめる) - recommend; encourage; offer

## Meaning

勧める is a transitive ichidan verb. It can recommend an action or item, encourage someone, or offer something for them to accept. The recipient takes に; a recommended or offered item takes を.

- 医者は私に運動するように勧めました。 (いしゃはわたしにうんどうするようにすすめました。) - The doctor advised me to exercise.
- 客にお茶を勧めました。 (きゃくにおちゃをすすめました。) - I offered the guest tea.

For an action, dictionary-form verb + ように勧める is useful. 本を勧める (ほんをすすめる) means "recommend a book."

## How the kanji combine

勧 contributes urging or encouraging and is read すす here; める completes the verb. Forms include 勧めます (すすめます), 勧めない (すすめない), and 勧めて (すすめて).

## Synonyms and antonyms

薦める (すすめる) is another spelling for recommending something or someone, such as a book or a candidate. The dictionary does not extend that spelling to the encouragement and offering senses taught here. [進める](進める.md), also すすめる, is a different verb meaning to advance or move something forward.

## Distinctive meaning

勧める does not establish that the other person accepted. Offering tea, recommending a book, and urging someone to exercise describe the speaker's action; the recipient can still decline. Keep the recommended thing or action separate from the person receiving the recommendation.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1595680, senses 1-3, including their spelling restrictions.

# 呼び掛ける (よびかける) - call out to; appeal; urge

## Meaning

呼び掛ける means to call out to or address someone, getting their
attention. It also means to appeal to people or urge their cooperation.
It is an ichidan verb: 呼び掛けます, 呼び掛けた, 呼び掛けない.

- 道の向こうにいる友達に呼び掛けました。 (みちのむこうにいるともだちによびかけました。) - I called out to my friend on the other side of the road.
- 住民に節水を呼び掛けました。 (じゅうみんにせっすいをよびかけました。) - We urged residents to conserve water.

The person addressed can take に. In the appeal construction,
the requested cooperation or action can take を, as 節水 does above.

## How the kanji combine

[呼](../kanji/呼.md)び is the stem of 呼ぶ (よぶ), call.
[掛](../kanji/掛.md)ける joins it in this native compound.
The compound directs a call toward someone; the independent "hang"
meaning of 掛ける is not a literal translation of the whole verb.
呼びかける is another recognized spelling.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[話しかける](話しかける.md) (はなしかける) concerns addressing
someone or beginning to talk to them.
[訴える](訴える.md) (うったえる) overlaps in appealing, while
[勧める](勧める.md) (すすめる) can encourage an action.
[呼び出す](呼び出す.md) (よびだす) focuses on summoning or
calling someone up, rather than necessarily appealing for cooperation.

## Distinctive meaning

A call to conserve water does not mean the residents have already
agreed or acted. The appeal can be directed to a group rather than
one nearby listener. Conversely, calling to a friend need not
be a public speech or a request for a campaign.
Do not translate every English "address" with this verb:
an address written on an envelope is not an act of 呼び掛ける.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1266280, senses 1-2.
Attachment examples: [Digital Daijisen](https://www.weblio.jp/content/呼び掛ける).

# 命令 (めいれい) - order; command

## Meaning

命令 is a noun for an order or command. 命令する means "order someone to do something."
A useful pattern is person + に + plain nonpast verb + ように命令する.

- 上司は部下に待つように命令しました。 (じょうしはぶかにまつようにめいれいしました。) - The supervisor ordered the subordinate to wait.
- コンピューターは命令を実行します。 (コンピューターはめいれいをじっこうします。) - The computer executes instructions.

The second example uses the computing sense: an instruction supplied to a computer.
命令に従う (めいれいにしたがう) means "obey an order," with に marking what is followed.

## How the kanji combine

[命](../kanji/命.md) has a command or mandate meaning as well as its familiar life meaning.
[令](../kanji/令.md) also contributes an order or directive. Their related meanings reinforce the command sense.
The readings are メイ + レイ; this word does not mean "an order about life" in every use.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[頼む](頼む.md) (たのむ), "ask; request," need not assert the authority associated with an order.
[注文](注文.md) (ちゅうもん) is an order for goods or services, a different meaning of English "order."
[従う](従う.md) (したがう) describes complying, not issuing the command.

## Distinctive meaning

Calling an instruction 命令 presents it as a command, not simply helpful advice.
This can matter in describing workplace or personal interactions.
In computing, however, the term is technical rather than a judgment about interpersonal tone.
The recipient and setting distinguish these uses.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1532160, senses 1-2.

# 意見 (いけん) — opinion

## Meaning

意見 is an opinion or view about a subject. Useful combinations are 意見を言う (いけんをいう), "state an opinion," and 意見を聞く (いけんをきく), "ask for/listen to an opinion."

この計画について、意見を聞かせてください。 (このけいかくについて、いけんをきかせてください。) — Please tell me your opinion about this plan.

## How the kanji combine

[意](../kanji/意.md) concerns thought or intention, and [見](../kanji/見.md) concerns seeing or a view. Together they suggest a considered view of something. Both use on-readings: い + けん.

## Synonyms and antonyms

考え (かんがえ) is broader: a thought, idea, or plan. [感想](感想.md) (かんそう) is an impression or reaction after an experience. Neither is always interchangeable with an opinion on a proposal.

## Distinctive meaning

The ordinary noun does not imply either agreement or disagreement. 私の意見 (わたしのいけん) means "my opinion." Be careful with 意見する: it can mean to admonish or remonstrate with someone, not simply the neutral act of expressing any opinion. For beginners, 意見を言う is the clearer neutral pattern.

# 招く (まねく) — invite

## Meaning

招く is a transitive godan verb meaning to invite in the sense taught here. A useful pattern is **person を + place に + 招く**:
invite someone to a place.

- 友達を家に招きました。 (ともだちをいえにまねきました。) — I invited a friend to my home.
- 夕食に先生を招きます。 (ゆうしょくにせんせいをまねきます。) — I will invite my teacher to dinner.

The past is 招いた (まねいた), and the negative is 招かない (まねかない).

## How the kanji combine

[招](../kanji/招.md) supplies the invitation idea. The final く is part of a native verb, not another component.
The on reading ショウ instead appears in 招待 (しょうたい), "invitation."

## Synonyms and antonyms

招待する (しょうたいする) also means inviting someone.
誘う (さそう) is useful for asking someone to join an activity:
友達を映画に誘う (ともだちをえいがにさそう), "invite a friend to a movie."
This is a useful contrast of situations, not a rule forbidding overlap between the verbs.

## Distinctive meaning

招く presents the invitation; it does not say the invited person accepted or arrived.
In the home example, the speaker is inviting someone as a guest, rather than merely proposing that they go somewhere together.
Other dictionary senses exist, but this article does not use them to blur the guest-invitation pattern.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entries 1349590 (sense 1), 1349610, 1541900.

# 招待 (しょうたい) — invitation

## Meaning

招待 means an invitation. 招待する means to invite someone as a guest. The person invited takes を; the event or destination takes に.

友達を家に招待しました。（ともだちをいえにしょうたいしました。） — I invited a friend to my home.

結婚式に招待されました。（けっこんしきにしょうたいされました。） — I was invited to a wedding.

## How the kanji combine

[招](../kanji/招.md) suggests inviting or beckoning, and [待](../kanji/待.md) contributes waiting or receiving. Both use on readings: しょう + たい. Learn the compound as inviting and receiving guests.

## Synonyms and antonyms

誘う（さそう） is broader: it can mean asking someone to join an activity. 招待 emphasizes treating them as a guest.

## Distinctive meaning

招待する is not simply telling someone to come. It presents an invitation to a hosted occasion or place. 招待状（しょうたいじょう） is a written invitation; 招待された uses the passive to describe receiving one.

# 推薦 (すいせん) - recommendation; endorsement

## Meaning

推薦 is a recommendation or endorsement of a person or thing as suitable.
推薦する is transitive: Xを推薦する means "recommend X."
A role can be marked with に, as in 会長に推薦する (かいちょうにすいせんする), "recommend for chairperson."

- 私は田中さんを会長に推薦します。 (わたしはたなかさんをかいちょうにすいせんします。) - I recommend Tanaka for chairperson.
- 先生からこの本を推薦されました。 (せんせいからこのほんをすいせんされました。) - My teacher recommended this book to me.

The passive in the second sentence presents the recommendation from the recipient's viewpoint.
推薦を受ける (すいせんをうける) means "receive a recommendation."

## How the kanji combine

推 contributes putting forward or supporting, and 薦 recommending.
Together they convey putting someone or something forward for consideration.
The on-readings are スイ + セン.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[勧める](勧める.md) (すすめる) is a broader everyday verb for recommending or encouraging.
[選ぶ](選ぶ.md) (えらぶ) means choosing; recommending a candidate does not mean the candidate has already been selected.
[紹介](紹介.md) (しょうかい) can introduce someone without endorsing them for a role.

## Distinctive meaning

推薦 carries a positive judgment of suitability, but it is not a guarantee of acceptance or success.
In educational or employment contexts, 推薦状 (すいせんじょう) is a letter of recommendation.
Check who recommends whom and for what: the particles make those relationships explicit.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1371170, sense 1.

# 提案 (ていあん) - proposal; suggestion

## Meaning

提案 is a proposal or suggestion presented for consideration. 提案する is transitive: the proposed idea takes を, and its recipient can take に. A plain verb plus ことを提案する expresses a proposed action.

- 会議で新しい方法を提案しました。 (かいぎであたらしいほうほうをていあんしました。) - I proposed a new method at the meeting.
- 先生に、発表を来週にすることを提案しました。 (せんせいに、はっぴょうをらいしゅうにすることをていあんしました。) - I suggested to the teacher that we give the presentation next week.

提案に賛成する (ていあんにさんせいする) means "agree with a proposal." Here に belongs to 賛成する, not to the act of proposing.

## How the kanji combine

提 contributes putting forward or presenting, and [案](../kanji/案.md) contributes a plan or idea. Together they describe putting an idea before others. The reading is テイ + アン.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[意見](意見.md) (いけん) is an opinion; it need not recommend an action. [計画](計画.md) (けいかく) is a plan, which may be the content of a proposal.

[命令](命令.md) (めいれい), "order; command," is a useful contrast in force, not an antonym.

## Distinctive meaning

A 提案 remains something to consider. It does not imply acceptance, authorization, or [実行](実行.md) (じっこう), "carrying out." The noun works for a practical everyday suggestion as well as an organizational proposal; its meaning does not require an elaborate written document.

# 支える (ささえる) - support; hold up

## Meaning

支える, read ささえる, is a transitive ichidan verb for supporting, holding up, or sustaining something. Mark the supported thing or person with **を**. The support may be physical, financial, or emotional.

- この柱が屋根を支えています。 (このはしらがやねをささえています。) - This pillar supports the roof.
- 家族が私を支えてくれました。 (かぞくがわたしをささえてくれました。) - My family supported me.

The past is 支えた (ささえた), and the negative is 支えない (ささえない). In the second example, くれました presents the support as something received with appreciation.

## How the kanji combine

[支](../kanji/支.md) supplies the support idea. In the spelling 支える, 支 is read ささ and える is written in kana. The ichidan stem used for conjugation is 支え (ささえ), formed by removing only the final る.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[助ける](助ける.md) (たすける) broadly means helping or rescuing. 支える highlights what keeps a person, structure, or activity from failing or collapsing. [援助](援助.md) (えんじょ) names assistance and can overlap in material support.

## Distinctive meaning

Do not read this support verb as "get blocked" or "choke." The separate verb つかえる means "get stuck" and is normally written in kana; its dictionary also lists 支える as a rare spelling. Shared written forms do not merge ささえる and つかえる into one reading or construction.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1310090, sense 1; contrast 1607170, sense 1 (つかえる).

# 注意 (ちゅうい) — attention, caution

## Meaning

注意 means attention or caution. With する, it can mean "pay attention" or "be careful." It can also refer to warning or reprimanding someone.

- 車に注意してください。 (くるまに ちゅういして ください。) — Please watch out for cars.
- 先生に注意されました。 (せんせいに ちゅういされました。) — I was told off by the teacher.

In the first example, に marks what to watch out for. In the passive second example, に marks the person who gave the reprimand.
The subject and the situation therefore matter: not every 注意する sentence means simply "be careful."

## How the kanji combine

[注](../kanji/注.md) contributes directing or concentrating, and [意](../kanji/意.md) contributes the mind or intention.
As a meaning aid, think "direct the mind toward something": a verb-and-object relationship.
The reading is on + on, チュウ + イ → ちゅうい.

## Synonyms and antonyms

- 気を付ける (きをつける), "be careful," overlaps with the caution sense. It does not replace 注意する when the intended meaning is "tell someone off."
- 不注意 (ふちゅうい), "carelessness, inattention," contrasts with paying attention. It is not the opposite of every warning or reprimand.

## Distinctive meaning

注意 on a sign is a request for caution, not an English "notice" meaning any announcement whatsoever.
The same word can describe your own attentiveness or another person's corrective warning. Learn the whole construction and its context.

# 激励 (げきれい) — encouragement; spurring on

## Meaning

激励 is encouragement that spurs someone on. It is a noun, and 激励する means "encourage" or "give a pep talk." The person or group encouraged can take を.

- 選手団を激励する。 (せんしゅだんをげきれいする。) — They encourage the team.
- 先生は学生たちを激励しました。 (せんせいはがくせいたちをげきれいしました。) — The teacher encouraged the students.

## How the kanji combine

激 contributes intensity or stirring up, and [励](../kanji/励.md) contributes encouraging. This is an intensifying combination, not a literal instruction to become violent. The readings are ゲキ + レイ.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[励ます](励ます.md) (はげます) is the native verb for encouraging or cheering someone on. [応援](応援.md) (おうえん) covers support and cheering, including practical backup as well as encouragement. The overlap is real: it is not a strict division between words and actions.

## Distinctive meaning

Learn both the noun 激励 and the verb 激励する. Encouraging someone to keep going is not the same as every kind of assistance, and the word does not guarantee success or an immediate improvement in the recipient's mood. Nor does every use require shouting or harsh treatment.

# 相談 (そうだん) — consultation; asking for advice

## Meaning

相談 is talking something over or asking someone for advice. Add する to make the verb.
Two useful frames are person + に + 相談する for consulting someone, and person + と + 相談する for discussing something together.

- 進路について先生に相談しました。 (しんろについてせんせいにそうだんしました。) — I consulted my teacher about my future course of study or career.
- 旅行の計画を家族と相談します。 (りょこうのけいかくをかぞくとそうだんします。) — I will discuss the travel plans with my family.

The topic can be marked with について, "about," or appear as an を-object, as in the second example.

## How the kanji combine

[相](../kanji/相.md) contributes an interpersonal or mutual association, and [談](../kanji/談.md) contributes talking or discussion.
The combination is an exchange about a matter, not just the physical act of speaking.
The on readings are ソウ + ダン.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[質問](質問.md) しつもん is a question or inquiry. Asking a specific factual question can be part of a consultation,
but 相談 often involves considering what to do.
[話す](話す.md) はなす is broader: people can talk without seeking advice or reaching a decision.

## Distinctive meaning

相談 does not require the participants to have equal expertise, nor does it guarantee that they agree.
先生に相談する can put a learner in the advice-seeking role.
For practical use, remember the topic and the person separately rather than translating the English "consult someone" word for word with を.

# 誘う (さそう) - invite; entice

## Meaning

誘う is a transitive godan verb meaning to invite someone to do something, or to entice or draw them in. Use person + を and activity/occasion + に.

- 友達を映画に誘いました。 (ともだちをえいがにさそいました。) - I invited my friend to a movie.
- 猫が魚のにおいに誘われて来ました。 (ねこがさかなのにおいにさそわれてきました。) - The cat came, drawn by the smell of fish.

The passive 誘われる (さそわれる) means "be invited/enticed." The past is 誘った (さそった), and the negative is 誘わない (さそわない).

The verb can also mean to evoke a response: 涙を誘う話 (なみだをさそうはなし), "a story that brings tears," names an emotional effect rather than an invitation.

## How the kanji combine

誘 writes the native verb stem さそ, followed by う. There is no multi-kanji compound. The spelling also supports another dictionary reading, いざなう; this card teaches さそう and its forms.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[招く](招く.md) (まねく) can mean inviting or welcoming someone. [招待](招待.md) (しょうたい) is an invitation or the act of inviting as a guest. 誘う readily describes asking a friend to join an activity, without specifying a hosted event.

## Distinctive meaning

An invitation does not establish acceptance: 誘ったけれど断られた (さそったけれどことわられた) means "I invited them, but they declined." The object also distinguishes meanings: invite a person, entice an animal, or evoke tears. Do not read the English "ask" as asking any kind of question.

# 警告 (けいこく) - warning; caution

## Meaning

警告 is a warning or caution about danger, a problem, or consequences. 警告する is a transitive する verb. Use **person に警告する** for the recipient, and **clause と警告する** to state the warning's content.

- 警察は住民に危険を警告しました。 (けいさつはじゅうみんにきけんをけいこくしました。) - The police warned residents of the danger.
- 画面に警告が出ています。 (がめんにけいこくがでています。) - A warning is showing on the screen.

The noun also fits 警告を受ける (けいこくをうける), "receive a warning." A warning may concern misconduct, but the word does not itself mean that a penalty has already been imposed.

## How the kanji combine

[警](../kanji/警.md) contributes alertness or warning; [告](../kanji/告.md) contributes telling or informing. Together they express informing someone so that they take warning. The on readings are ケイ + コク.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[注意](注意.md) (ちゅうい) includes attention and caution; 注意する can overlap with warning someone. 忠告 (ちゅうこく), "advice; admonition," can also overlap, but ordinary helpful advice is not automatically a 警告.

## Distinctive meaning

Translate 警告 as "warning," not as a general-purpose "advice." Advice about choosing a pleasant restaurant need not warn of anything. 警告 draws attention to something the recipient should avoid or take seriously, whether spoken by a person or displayed by a device.

# 進める (すすめる) - move forward; carry forward

## Meaning

進める is a transitive ichidan verb meaning to move something forward or carry work or a plan forward. Mark what is advanced with を.

- 会議を予定どおりに進めましょう。 (かいぎをよていどおりにすすめましょう。) - Let's proceed with the meeting as planned.
- 時計を一時間進めました。 (とけいをいちじかんすすめました。) - I set the clock forward one hour.

仕事を進める (しごとをすすめる) means "make progress with the work." The past is 進めた (すすめた); the negative is 進めない (すすめない).

## How the kanji combine

[進](../kanji/進.md) supplies the forward-progress idea, and める completes the native verb. Compare the related intransitive [進む](進む.md) (すすむ): 仕事が進む, "the work progresses."

## Synonyms and antonyms

[続ける](続ける.md) (つづける), "continue," emphasizes not stopping; 進める emphasizes advancing the activity.

[勧める](勧める.md) has the same reading すすめる but means to recommend or encourage. 本を勧める recommends a book; it does not mean moving it forward.

## Distinctive meaning

The object need not physically move: discussions, preparations, and research can be advanced. Conversely, 進める is not a general substitute for "promote" in every English sentence. Learn the object and verb together. The を/が contrast is especially useful: someone advances the plan with を進める, while the plan itself progresses with が進む.
